name: Ishtaria
tagline: A persistent, federated, Earth-sized virtual planet.
home_title: Ishtaria – a virtual planet of your own
home_lead: Explore a persistent planet with a fully customisable avatar. Every server hosts an independent world; portals connect worlds that have agreed to trust each other.
feat_1_p: The server owns the world and decides outcomes. The client only sends intentions, so balances, inventory and movement cannot be forged.
feat_2_p: No central universe and no blockchain. Servers make bilateral agreements and hand players over through discrete, signed portals.
feat_3_p: Terrain is generated deterministically from a seed. Only the changes players make are stored.
feat_4_p: Server, client, generator, content and protocol are open. Run your own world and tell stories on it with datadisks.
shot_1_alt: The stepped tower of Ishtar in the sacred precinct of Uruk, with the goddess and her priests on its top platform.
shot_2_alt: The great market of Uruk, with its crowd of named townspeople.
status_p: Ishtaria is under active development. Accounts, character creation, walking, gathering, towns and story datadisks work; first physical landing, sailing and federation handovers are not finished yet. Expect rough edges.
dl_lead: Ishtaria is distributed as Debian packages for Debian and Ubuntu on x86-64. Other systems are not supported.
dl_play_p: Install the client, start it and enter the address of a server.
dl_host_p: Install the server and its tools; it needs PostgreSQL. See the documentation for setup.
dl_req_p: Debian 13 (trixie) or Ubuntu 26.04 (resolute), x86-64, a GPU with Vulkan or OpenGL support for the client, PostgreSQL for the server.
pkg_ishtaria-admin: Text-mode administration of a world server.
pkg_ishtaria-content: Base content pack: species, items, recipes, biomes.
pkg_ishtaria-datadisk-endland: A small example datadisk: one town with a tavern.
pkg_ishtaria-datadisk-gilgamesh: The Epic of Gilgamesh, the main story datadisk: Uruk and the Early Dynastic world on a reconstructed Earth.
pkg_ishtaria-datadisk-tutorial: The tutorial datadisk: guided lessons for every implemented feature.
footer_license: Server AGPL-3.0, code MIT, content and documentation CC BY-SA 4.0. Artwork credits are listed in the client.
dl_direct_p: Standalone client builds from the release. The Debian package above is the supported way to install; the other builds are untested and the Windows and macOS builds are not code-signed, so expect a system warning.
play_lead: The same client as the desktop game, built for the browser (HTML5 / WebAssembly). Nothing to install: enter the address of a world server and play.
play_open_here_p: This site hosts a world. One click loads the browser client and connects to it.
play_how_p: The page loads the client (a large download on the first visit, then it is cached) and connects to the server you name. The address is taken from the link, so a world can publish a ready link such as /play/?server=https://world.example.
play_https_h: The server has to allow the browser
play_https_p: A page served over https can only reach servers over https, and the server must answer browsers from this site: either the operator puts it behind this site's reverse proxy (then the link is /play/?server=/server) or it sends the headers a browser needs. A world that does neither cannot be played in the browser; use the desktop client for it.
play_limits_p: The browser build uses the simpler WebGL 2 renderer, so the terrain and the sky look a little different, and it needs a recent browser and a GPU with WebGL 2. Only Debian and Ubuntu are supported for the desktop client; the browser build runs wherever the browser does, without support.
play_host_h: Offering it from your own site
play_host_p: The files come in the package ishtaria-client-web; the portal serves them under /play/ when it is installed.
pkg_ishtaria-client-web: The game client for the browser (HTML5 / WebAssembly).
story_p: The first full story disk retells the Epic of Gilgamesh on a reconstructed Early Dynastic Earth. You begin as the hunter at a water-hole and walk to Uruk, a walled city drawn from a plan of the real one: ziggurats, thousands of houses, canals, markets and the Euphrates. The people of Uruk speak Czech or English, and what they tell you follows the story you have lived so far.
shot_3_alt: The quay of Uruk at the river gate, seen from the far bank of the Euphrates.
shot_4_alt: Talking to an elder: every character has a portrait, and the story is told in decision trees.
shot_5_alt: The map of Uruk: walls and gates, streets, houses, canals and the Euphrates.
support_p: Ishtaria is built by a small team in its spare time and it is free to play. If you enjoy it, you can support the development on Patreon. Money is not the only way to help: report bugs, translate the game, write a story datadisk or send a patch (each repository has a CONTRIBUTING.md), and tell other players about it.
start_p: New here? These are real gaps in the current game, each a good first contribution. Ask in an issue before you begin a bigger one.
start_1: Play the first quest of the Gilgamesh datadisk and report what is confusing, broken or ugly (an issue with a screenshot is a real contribution).
start_2: Proofread the English and Czech texts, or add a third language to the client's translations.
start_3: Write a small story datadisk: a place, a character and a short dialogue (the format is described in the protocol repository and checked by a validator).
start_4: Add a "Tell me about yourself" knowledge card to the characters of Uruk that do not have one yet.
start_5: Add counter achievements, for example felling a hundred trees (there are only one-time milestones now).
start_6: Show the mood of a character above their head: the Emotes Pack is bundled but not used yet.
start_7: Let a character sleep in a placed bedroll, and give placed objects collisions.
start_8: Lay roads from the other gates of Uruk to the neighbouring cities (the generator tool already exists, only the legs are missing).
start_9: Add blocking of players and message requests to the chat.
start_10: Improve the tests: more PostgreSQL integration tests for the server, or visual checks of the client windows.
